title: Major Depressive Disorder: Diagnosis and First‑Line Pharmacotherapy
summary: Concise, evidence-informed guide to diagnosing MDD and initiating first-line pharmacotherapy. Emphasizes DSM-5/operational criteria, risk stratification, shared decision-making, SSRI/SNRI selection, dosing, titration, monitoring, and when to combine with psychotherapy.
clinicalQuestion: How should clinicians diagnose major depressive disorder and select first-line pharmacotherapy in adults?

heroStats.label: Diagnostic threshold
heroStats.value: ≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks incl. depressed mood or anhedonia [1]

heroStats.label: First‑line meds
heroStats.value: SSRIs favored for tolerability; SNRIs, others reasonable alternatives [2], [3]

heroStats.label: Effectiveness
heroStats.value: Escitalopram suitable first‑line in moderate–severe MDD [4]

heroStats.label: Nonpharmacologic
heroStats.value: EBT psychotherapy comparable to meds for many patients [5]

keyMoments.title: Confirm the diagnosis
keyMoments.body: Use operational DSM criteria: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks with functional impairment** and rule out bipolar, substances, and medical mimics [1].

keyMoments.title: Stratify severity and suicide risk
keyMoments.body: Assess severity, comorbidity, and **acute suicide risk** to determine outpatient vs higher level of care and urgency of pharmacotherapy [2].

keyMoments.title: Select first‑line therapy
keyMoments.body: Start with an **SSRI** based on tolerability and safety; **escitalopram** supported as a suitable first‑line option in moderate–severe MDD [4], with alternatives per patient factors [2], [3].

keyMoments.title: Combine with psychotherapy when feasible
keyMoments.body: **Evidence‑based psychotherapies** (CBT, IPT, BA) are as effective as medication for many, and combination improves outcomes in moderate–severe or chronic MDD [5].

keyMoments.title: Plan for measurement‑based care
keyMoments.body: Set a follow‑up schedule, use standardized scales, **titrate every 2–4 weeks**, and adjust if <20–25% improvement by 4–6 weeks [2].

sections.title: Operational Diagnostic Approach
sections.blurb: Define MDD using DSM-style operational criteria and exclude differentials before initiating therapy.

steps.title: Apply DSM operational criteria
steps.body: Require **≥5 depressive symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including **depressed mood or anhedonia**, with distress/impairment; exclude bereavement-only presentations, mania/hypomania, and psychosis [1].

steps.title: Screen and stage severity
steps.body: Use PHQ‑9 or similar to quantify baseline severity and to facilitate **measurement‑based care**; document functional impairment and episode specifiers (anxious distress, melancholic, peripartum, seasonal) [2].

steps.title: Rule out medical and substance causes
steps.body: Targeted history, medications/substances review, and selective labs (TSH, CBC, CMP, B12/folate as indicated). Evaluate for bipolar spectrum to avoid antidepressant‑induced mania [2].

sections.title: First‑Line Pharmacotherapy Selection
sections.blurb: SSRIs are generally preferred for tolerability; choose agent and dose by patient profile, prior response, comorbidities, and drug–drug interactions.

steps.title: Start with an SSRI for most
steps.body: Guidance and reviews favor **SSRIs** as first‑line due to **higher tolerability** and safety in overdose compared with older classes [2], while acknowledging no single class is universally superior in efficacy [3].

steps.title: Consider escitalopram as a default option
steps.body: Network/meta-analytic data support **escitalopram** as a suitable first‑line for moderate–severe MDD, with favorable acceptability; reported outcomes favor response and remission vs several comparators [4].

steps.title: Individualize alternatives
steps.body: SNRIs (e.g., venlafaxine, duloxetine) for comorbid pain or prior SSRI nonresponse; bupropion for low energy and sexual side effects avoidance; mirtazapine for insomnia/weight loss. Balance benefits with patient risks and preferences [2], [3].

steps.title: Combine with psychotherapy as indicated
steps.body: For mild–moderate MDD, **psychotherapy alone** may be comparable to meds; for moderate–severe or chronic MDD, **combination** improves outcomes and adherence [5].

sections.title: Starting Doses, Titration, and Monitoring
sections.blurb: Initiate low, titrate based on tolerability and symptom change, and monitor systematically.

cards.title: SSRI starting and typical ranges
items: Escitalopram: start 5–10 mg daily; typical 10–20 mg [4], [2]
Sertraline: start 25–50 mg; typical 50–200 mg [2]
Fluoxetine: start 10–20 mg; typical 20–60 mg [2]
Citalopram: start 10–20 mg; typical 20–40 mg (QT caution at higher doses) [2]

cards.title: SNRIs and other options
items: Venlafaxine XR: start 37.5–75 mg; typical 75–225 mg [2]
Duloxetine: start 30 mg; typical 60–120 mg [2]
Bupropion SR/XL: start 100–150 mg; typical 300–450 mg/day (avoid in seizure/eating disorders) [2]
Mirtazapine: start 7.5–15 mg; typical 15–45 mg (sedating, weight gain) [2]

cards.title: Follow‑up cadence
items: Reassess at 2 weeks for tolerability; 4–6 weeks for early efficacy [2]
If <20–25% improvement by 4–6 weeks: optimize dose or switch [2]
Aim for remission (PHQ‑9 ≤4) rather than partial response [2]

cards.title: Safety monitoring
items: Suicidality, especially early in treatment and in younger adults [2]
Activation/anxiety, GI effects, sexual dysfunction (SSRIs/SNRIs) [2]
Blood pressure (SNRIs), QT risk (citalopram), hyponatremia in older adults [2]

cards.title: Special populations and cautions
items: Pregnancy/lactation: weigh risks/benefits; sertraline commonly used [2]
Bipolar risk: screen before starting antidepressants [2]
Recent MI/arrhythmia: prefer sertraline; avoid high‑dose citalopram (QT) [2]

cards.title: If inadequate response
items: Confirm adherence, diagnosis, dose, and comorbidities [2]
Switch within class or to SNRI/bupropion/mirtazapine [2], [3]
Augment with psychotherapy; pharmacologic augmentation per guidance and FDA trial principles in treatment‑resistant settings [6], [2]

sections.title: Regulatory Guidance Touchpoints (for interpretation of evidence)
sections.blurb: Understanding FDA guidance helps contextualize endpoints and response definitions in antidepressant trials.

steps.title: Primary endpoints and timing
steps.body: Trials typically evaluate **change in validated depression scales** (e.g., MADRS, HAM‑D) over 6–8 weeks; response is often **≥50% reduction** and remission based on scale thresholds [6].

steps.title: Populations and designs
steps.body: Guidance supports monotherapy, adjunctive, and combination designs, with attention to **placebo control**, enrichment strategies, and safety signal detection for suicidality and activation [6].
